text: **A store written by an older schema is DETECTED, and is either migrated or refused -- never silently opened.** Found live by dc 2026-08-15 via `int dogfood`, on a v3 project created ~40 minutes before the AC-enum collapse landed: `intent st list --status all` fails with `sqlite: no such column: state`, because **`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` makes the DDL a NO-OP against an existing database**, so `Store::open()` returns SUCCESS on a store it cannot read. **The open path succeeding on an unreadable database is the defect**; the query failure is only where it surfaces, and the distance between broken and found-out is however long until somebody runs a verb naming the new column. **Detection is impossible today**: no `user_version`, no `schema_version`, nothing a migration could dispatch on even once one exists. This is the FIRST live instance of the class D01's reversal created -- `store.rs:4` already states "MIGRATIONS ARE NORMAL, so there is no rebuild-instead-of-migrating story", so **the policy was written and the mechanism was not built**, and D36 removed the escape hatch the same morning by ruling `rm intent.db` out of existence. Requires: a stamped schema version in the store; an open path that compares it and refuses or migrates; and, per `IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001`, **a remedy on the refusal** -- "your database predates a schema change" is a better sentence than `no such column: state at offset 23` even while no migrator exists. **The recovery path is the EXTRACT, not the snapshot** (see D35): restoring a D35 snapshot taken before the change reproduces the old schema, so re-ingest from the `.json`/`.md` extract is what actually survives schema evolution. **VERIFIED 2026-08-15 (vc) at `523b34e8`, built before it was contracted: `cargo test -p intentsvcs --test store_schema_version` -> 6 passed, and the discriminating case is the one this row demanded -- the fixture lays down the OLD `criteria` shape, `Store::open` returns `Err` with no query run, `SchemaUnstamped` and `SchemaMismatch` are separate variants, and `remedy()` is non-empty and distinct per variant.** Two things the build got right that this row did not ask for: the mismatch remedy names WHICH END can move (there is no migrating a store backwards into a binary that never heard of its shape), and the `Sqlite` remedy carries D36's warning explicitly -- "do NOT delete the store -- it is the source of truth, not a cache". **THE LIMIT, raised by cc and priced here rather than discovered later: this AC buys DETECTION, never recoverability for what already exists.** A migration ladder can only start at 1, because `user_version = 0` is not schema zero -- it is the ABSENCE of one, permanently spoken for by SQLite's default -- so a pre-stamp store records nothing a migrator could dispatch on and is refused forever. dc's dogfood DB is in that set. That is the correct outcome under D34 (the extract is the interchange, the DB is per-machine) and the `SchemaUnstamped` remedy says so honestly rather than inventing a recovery command, but **anything never synced out of a pre-stamp store exists only there**. Read this row as "no store is ever silently misread", never as "no store is ever lost"
